title: A tour of the workspace
summary: Find your way around Phoenix: the toolbox and its flyouts, the edit bar and stage controls, the timeline, the Properties panel's tabs, the Library, Color and Swatches panels, and workspaces.

steps.title: Welcome
steps.text:
This lesson is a quick walk around the Phoenix window, so you know where everything is before you start animating.

Phoenix has opened a new document to look around in. Most steps just point something out: read them and click Next. A few ask you to try something, and move on by themselves when you do.

steps.title: The toolbox
steps.text:
The drawing and selection tools live here. Each button is a slot. Many slots hold several related tools, and show the one you used last.

Right-click the toolbox and choose Edit Toolbar to arrange the slots your way.

steps.title: Open a flyout
steps.text:
Press and hold the slot with the Rectangle and Oval tools. A flyout opens with the other tools in that slot.

Choose the PolyStar tool. The slot now shows it, so it is one click away next time.

steps.title: Stroke color
steps.text: Under the tools are the colors new artwork is drawn with. The outlined square is the stroke color: click it to pick a new one.

steps.title: Fill color
steps.text:
The solid square is the fill color. The two small buttons with them set black and white, or swap stroke and fill.

Below them is the Object Drawing button, J, which the lesson Merge and object drawing explains.

steps.title: The stage and pasteboard
steps.text: The white rectangle is the stage: what is on it is what your movie shows. The gray area around it is the pasteboard, where artwork can wait off screen, ready to enter.

steps.title: Pan the view
steps.text: Press H for the Hand tool and drag the stage around. With any other tool, holding Space does the same.

steps.title: The zoom box
steps.text: The edit bar above the stage holds the stage controls. This box shows the magnification: type a percentage, or click its arrows to step through the presets. Ctrl+= and Ctrl+- zoom in and out too.

steps.title: Magnification presets
steps.text: This arrow opens the presets: Fit in Window, Show All and fixed sizes. Choose 200% to get close.

steps.title: Fit the stage again
steps.text: Press Ctrl+2, or choose View > Magnification > Fit in Window, to see the whole stage again.

steps.title: Center the stage
steps.text: This button brings the stage back to the middle of the view after panning, keeping the magnification.

steps.title: Turn the view
steps.text: This button picks the Rotation tool (Shift+H), which turns your view of the stage the way you would turn a sheet of paper. Once the view is turned, the button shows the angle and a click sets it straight. Turning the view never changes the artwork.

steps.title: Content outside the stage
steps.text: This menu chooses what happens to artwork out on the pasteboard: Show it, Dim it, or Clip it away so you see only what the movie will show.

steps.title: Edit Symbols
steps.text:
The left of the edit bar shows what you are editing: the scene, and the symbols you have gone into. Click a name to go back up to it.

At its right, Edit Symbols lists the library's symbols to open one directly. Edit > Edit Symbols (Ctrl+E) opens the selected instance's symbol, or takes you back to the document.

steps.title: The timeline
steps.text: The timeline holds the layers on the left and their frames on the right. Above the frames are the transport buttons: first frame, step back, Play and step forward. Enter plays and stops.

steps.title: Onion skin and loop
steps.text: This button turns on onion skinning, showing the frames around the playhead faintly on the stage. Right-click it for its settings. The button beside it loops playback.

steps.title: Frame view
steps.text: This menu sets how the frames look: their width, the height of the rows, thumbnails of the artwork, and time in seconds. Ctrl+wheel over the frames zooms them.

steps.title: Add a layer
steps.text:
Under the layer list are buttons for a new layer, a new folder and delete. Click New Layer now.

Double-click a layer's name to rename it.

steps.title: Properties: the Tool tab
steps.text: The Properties panel has four tabs along its top: Tool, Object, Frame and Doc. Click Tool: it holds the settings of the tool in use, such as its color and style and the tool's own options.

steps.title: Object and Frame
steps.text:
Click the tabs as you read. Object shows what is selected on the stage: position and size, and for a symbol instance its color effect, looping and filters.

Frame shows the frame at the playhead: its label, its tween and ease, and its sound.

steps.title: Doc
steps.text: Doc holds the document's settings: the stage's width and height, its color, and the frame rate.

steps.title: The Library
steps.text: The Library keeps the document's symbols, bitmaps and sounds. Drag an item onto the stage to place an instance of it; double-click one to edit it. Ctrl+L opens it.

steps.title: The Color panel
steps.text: The Color panel sets what new artwork is filled with: a solid color, a linear or radial gradient, or a bitmap. Apply to Selection fills the selected shapes with it.

steps.title: Swatches
steps.text: Swatches are the document's saved colors. Click one to make it the fill color; its menu sorts them and brings color tables in and out.

steps.title: The Window menu
steps.text:
Every panel is in the Window menu, ticked when open. Choose one to open it or bring it forward.

Window > Workspaces switches between whole layouts: Essentials, Animator, Designer and Classic. Arrange the panels your way and choose New Workspace to keep it.

steps.title: Hide the panels
steps.text: Press F4 to hide every panel and see the stage alone. Press F4 again to bring them back.

steps.title: That's the tour
steps.text:
You have seen the toolbox and its flyouts, the edit bar and stage controls, the timeline, the Properties tabs, the Library, Color and Swatches panels, and workspaces.

Next, try Merge and object drawing to learn how shapes you draw combine, or Your first animation if you have not made one yet.
